##### August 2025: SoWork 2.0 & The Dark Mode Debut

August was a milestone month for us as we transitioned to SoWork v2.0: The Glow Up Edition. We focused on core utility—bringing back favorite features like Mini-Mode and finally launching the #1 most requested feature in our history: Dark Mode. [...] Mobile App Upgrades: Mobile users on iOS and Android can now share their screens, swipe up in meetings to access chat, update text statuses, and view complete working hours and birthdays on teammate profiles.
 Customizable Home Sidebar: Drag, reorder, and collapse sidebar sections (Collaboration Hours, Meetings, Online, Offline) to customize your layout.
 Multi-User Whiteboard Drawing: Fixed a canvas bug so multiple teammates can draw on the meeting whiteboard simultaneously without interrupting each other's strokes.
 Camera Privacy Fix: Resolved an issue on the Desktop App to ensure camera hardware is fully released and indicator lights turn off immediately when video is disabled. [...] Revamped AI Meeting Library: Enjoy a faster, redesigned layout featuring custom collections, updated permissions, read/unread syncing, and improved browsing across both desktop and mobile devices.
 Google Drive Integration: Now live for all accounts! Connect Google Drive to share, attach, and access workspace documents directly inside your virtual office.
 Custom Video Backgrounds: Paid and trial users can now upload custom 16:9 images to serve as personal video backgrounds across all rooms and meeting sessions.
 Quick Chat Toolbar: Read and send meeting chat messages directly from the bottom toolbar without opening the full chat panel or taking your eyes off the office.

## Why teams look for a SoWork alternative

SoWork is a 2.5D virtual office: avatars move around an isometric world, conversations open by proximity, and paid plans add Slack-style chat and AI meeting summaries. It is one of the lowest-cost options in the category, with a free plan for up to 10 members. Teams usually move on for one of these reasons:

 The game look. An isometric world works for a small internal team. It reads differently in front of clients, candidates and executives.
 Avatars are position, not presence. You can see where someone is on the map, not whether they are actually there.
 Free plan limits. SoWork's free plan caps each meeting at 30 minutes and leaves out recording, analytics and AI.
 Scale. Teams over 100 move to SoWork's custom Enterprise plan. [...] ## How to choose

 You want real presence and a professional office: Katmai.
 You want to stay with avatars: Gather or Kumospace.
 You want rooms and an all-in-one tool: Roam.
 You need open source or self-hosting: WorkAdventure.
 You want the lowest-cost place to hang out: Flat.social.

## FAQ

What is the best alternative to SoWork?

For teams that want an office that looks and feels like a real one, Katmai: a photorealistic 3D office with live video, running in a browser. For teams that want to stay with avatars, Gather and Kumospace are the closest matches. For a room-based office bundled with chat and scheduling, Roam.
